title: Declaring an abstract method inside a class
answer: If a class declares an abstract method, that class must itself be declared abstract. An abstract method has no implementation body, so a concrete class containing one would promise that instances are fully usable even though required behavior is missing. A concrete subclass must implement the method unless that subclass also remains abstract.
